method: Ten deterministic rules, each computed from named fields in the Almanac shelf, the client profile, the Almanac page data and the curated opportunity register. Every number on the page is computed here; the page performs no arithmetic. Nothing on this page is written advice or model-generated prose. Eligibility is read from the Almanac shelf and never recomputed, and the warehouse is never queried.

headline.note: Read from the Almanac page data. Not recounted here, and not derived from the register's own row totals, which are stated limits rather than a result.

confidentiality_guard.rule: open_opportunities_curated is a SHARED shelf. Rows whose found_for_this_client is false belong to another client and are dropped. Emitted rows are built from an explicit field allowlist, so curator free text cannot reach the page even if a new leak phrasing appears.
confidentiality_guard.note: Every figure in this block was measured against the rows in this file, not declared from a constant. Fields beyond the emit-time allowlist are prior funder attributes added by R4 from this client's own EIN-verified history; none of them originates in the shared register.

rules.sentence: Your filed NTEE code is B05 (Education), and it is what the matching runs on. 40 of the 40 prospective funders the shelf returned were reached because they fund peers in that same band, and 40 of the 40 federal opportunities it returned carry the ED category. rules.sentence: You have already received $540,000 from 3 funders whose register-recorded funding geography names Dallas, TX, and your survey describes real programming and partnerships there. 51 rows on the shared register are nonetheless barred for you on geography, because your filed address reads as a single market.
rules.stated_limit: Two limits, and neither is in the client-facing sentence. First, the curated tier this rule counts over is 175 rows, which is the size of the CURATED SHELF for this client and not the size of the opportunity register, which is far larger; the shelf is that size because the register's geography column resolves at STATE level only, so a row is selected for being open in Texas rather than for being open in Austin. Second, that geography column records the OPPORTUNITY'S FUNDING GEOGRAPHY, not the funder's headquarters, and some rows state both in one string. A funder matched here funds INTO the named market; it is not necessarily seated there, and the sentence says funding geography for that reason.
notes: The sentence names only the secondary markets a register row actually matched. Markets on file with no matching register row are carried in the numbers block as secondary_markets_with_no_register_match rather than being named as though they had produced the dollars.

rules.headline: Federal eligibility is inferred rather than published on part of your tier
rules.trigger: federal rows are open to you, you have screening criteria on file, and at least one open federal row carries eligibility_basis 'inferred from opportunity text'
key_numbers: 39 federal opportunities open to you as of August 7, 2026
8 of them carry inferred rather than published eligibility
5 screening criteria on file

client_screening_criteria: business practices contributing to racial inequity
surveillance technologies disproportionately impacting marginalized communities
numbers.client_verbatim_caution: Also... we need to be careful with government grants that harm organization led by black women.

rules.sentence: 39 federal opportunities are open to you as of August 7, 2026, and on 8 of them the eligibility line was inferred from the opportunity text rather than coded by the publisher, so whether you qualify is a reading of the notice and not a published fact. You gave us 5 screening criteria and one explicit caution, and the federal tier carries no field in which a screen against them could be recorded, so nothing on it has been checked against your criteria by anything but a person.
rules.stated_limit: Federal rows come from Grants.gov and carry no client verdict of any kind. The union of keys across all 40 of them is agency, award_ceiling, award_floor, close_date, cost_sharing_required, eligibility_basis, expected_awards, funding_categories, international_flag, opportunity_number, post_date, program_funding, scope_note, source, title, which contains none of client_barred, found_for_this_client, client_screen, barred_reason. That absence is a property of the SOURCE SCHEMA and would hold for every client on every run, so it is recorded here as a limit and is deliberately not what makes this rule fire. What makes it fire is the inferred-eligibility count, which is measured and can be zero.
notes: Counts run over rows OPEN at the generation date. Counting over all 40 rows would import rows whose close date has already passed.
